grammar.title: 2A: Present perfect and past simple
grammar.explanation:
We use **have / has + past participle** to talk about our body and our life. We do not say when it happened.

We also use **have / has + past participle** for a new action with a result now. Your hand is clean because you washed it.

Use **just** for a very short time ago, **already** when it is done, and **yet** in questions and negative sentences.

Use the past simple when we say **when** it happened. Words like **yesterday** and **last week** need the past simple.

Never use **have / has** with **yesterday** or **last week**. That is wrong.
examples: I *have washed* my hair. (we do not say when)
She *has hurt* her leg. (her leg hurts now)
We *have just closed* our eyes. (a very short time ago)
They *have already* brushed their hair. (it is done)
Have you *washed* your hands *yet*? (a question with yet)
I *have never broken* my arm. (never in my life)
He *hurt* his back last week. (we say when: last week)
She *washed* her foot yesterday. (we say when: yesterday)
I *touched* my nose this morning. (finished action with a time)
You *have hurt* your mouth. (no time, the result is now)
